name: Dog
description: The body a player is, in the dog game: a low-poly Bernese mountain dog of 1,500 flat-shaded triangles with its tricolour coat as a palette in vertex colours and no texture, skinned to Kimi's 38 canine joints (hips, two spine segments, chest, neck, head, nose, jaw, two eyes, two-bone ears, a four-bone tail, fore legs of scapula, upper, lower, paw and toe, hind legs of upper, lower, hock, paw and toe), with the twelve clips a dog needs before any object speaks. The dog wears nothing: its collar, harness and packs are separate meshes on the same joints and ship as their own asset. The clips are authored on a control rig built to an animator's checklist and sampled onto the joints: the four gaits plant each paw on the ground with two keys, so a foot in a stance does not slide, and the speed each gait was authored for comes out of that geometry and is stated per clip.

sockets.name: mouth
sockets.description: Under the nose, at the tip of the jaw. The one thing movement.carry_in_mouth holds rides here, so it follows the jaw through a sniff, a bark and a drag. Parented to the jaw's deform bone.

sockets.name: collar
sockets.description: The throat, on the underside of the neck, where a collar's ring hangs and a leash clips. Parented to the neck's deform bone.

sockets.name: back
sockets.description: The top of the back behind the withers, measured off the body's surface, where a blanket or a pack is carried. Parented to the second spine segment's deform bone.

sockets.name: head_top
sockets.description: Crown of the head, between the ears, measured off the body's surface. Parented to the head's deform bone.

animations.name: idle
animations.description: One slow breath in the ribs, the weight easing from side to side, a glance left that the ears lead, a tail that wags from its root with each joint a little later.

animations.name: walk
animations.description: Four-beat lateral sequence: hind left, fore left, hind right, fore right, five frames apart. Each paw planted for 12 of 20 frames over a 0.38 m stance: authored for 0.76 m/s.

animations.name: trot
animations.description: Diagonal pairs half a cycle apart, each paw planted for 5 of 10 frames over a 0.40 m stance: authored for 1.92 m/s.

animations.name: run
animations.description: Rotary gallop: the hind pair a frame apart, then the fore pair a frame apart, the back rounding and flattening under them. Each paw planted for 4 of 10 frames over a 0.50 m stance: authored for 3.0 m/s.

animations.name: drag
animations.description: A walk with the weight back and the head low: the mouth is on something heavier than the dog lifts. Each paw planted for 16 of 24 frames over a 0.28 m stance: authored for 0.42 m/s. movement.carry_in_mouth's dragSpeedFactor is why it is slow.

animations.name: sniff
animations.description: Nose down on a scent: the front folds over planted paws, the neck drops and the nose sweeps side to side with the head a beat behind. The mouth socket comes down to within a few centimetres of the ground.

animations.name: sniff_air
animations.description: Nose up, on the wind: the head lifts, the mouth socket to about 0.88 m, and casts slowly.

animations.name: dig
animations.description: The fore paws scrape alternately along the ground, the chest low, the rump up, the head down watching the hole, the tail up. One cycle is one scrape of each paw; housing.den_and_cache counts the seconds.

animations.name: sit
animations.description: A small rise, then down onto the haunches a little past the pose and back up into it, and held: the rump to the ground, the hocks laid down behind flat paws, the fore paws stepping back one after the other.

animations.name: lie
animations.description: The sphinx: the front goes down first, the rear follows, fore legs out in front on their elbows, hocks on the ground, and the head comes down toward the paws and settles. What housing.den_and_cache's rest looks like.

animations.name: bark
animations.description: A dip, the head thrown up with the jaw open 32 degrees and the fore paws off the ground, past the pose, then shut. The brick drops what the mouth holds on a bark, so the open jaw is also what the player sees.

animations.name: mark
animations.description: The weight goes left, the right hind paw lifts out and up, holds while the body sinks a little on three legs, and comes down.

source.tool: Tripo API (the body this one is derived from, and the segmentation that split off the gear), Kimi's joints and weights, and blender-mcp-asset-pipeline 1.0.3 on Blender 4.4.3 (the low-poly body, the control rig, the clips, the export)
source.sourceFile: Riverside Bernese Dog — Base Rig.blend, 35256608 bytes, sha256 cb33715c12010ab2e18e126af0155e93c11c9f08eec9ed03c1f9fc80bf042743, Kimi's master of 9 Nov 2026; not in either repository, named by hash in the script

provenance: The yard (game-architect-studio #150) drew its dog as nine boxes turned as one, which is an honest grey-box and cannot sit, dig or put its nose down. Five bodies followed in the studio's build script on 9 Nov 2026 before this one: the boxes rigged as they stood, a voxel-remeshed shell of them, a lofted tube body, Kimi's first Tripo generation of the concept painting (which wore its gear), and Kimi's bare Tripo body on her own 144-bone rig. Alexander then asked for a truly low-poly dog, faceted with a flat palette, on a rig done properly, and shared the transcripts of P2Design's animation course to learn it from. What is Kimi's and kept: her 38 deform joints by name and rest pose, her weights, and her three gear meshes on those joints (her master is appended by sha256). Rights to Tripo output rest with the generating account under Tripo's terms, to be confirmed against the plan tier before the game is published. What is derived: this body is her bare shell voxel-remeshed into one closed surface, decimated with left-right symmetry and extra budget on the head, flat-shaded, each face coloured from her coat snapped to a five-colour palette, her weights carried across by nearest surface point (four at most, normalised). What is built here from scratch: the control layer, to the checklist an animator works from in that course's squirrel rig. Every deform joint copies a twin with its exact rest matrix; torso, neck, head, limbs and tail are stretch segments between joint tweaks; hips and chest are two pivots at the centre of gravity that move, rotate and scale, with the joints between following half-way so the back bends as a curve; the head rides a socket that takes the chest's position always and its rotation only by a head_follow property; four IK paws on scale-cancelling sockets with poles and 5% stretch, a one-channel foot roll with a toe pivot and a heel pivot, a hock control, toe controls; an FK tail on a tail_follow socket; hide_legs and hide_tail masks; unkeyable channels locked and a keying set of exactly the rest. The build proves, before any clip is keyed, that at rest every joint sits on Kimi's rest pose and that each control moves the mesh the way its name says. The clips are authored the two ways the course teaches and sampled onto the joints by the exporter: gaits layered one channel at a time with a planted paw as two vector-handled keys and the other paws as the same curves shifted by their phase, overlap down the tail and ears as one curve copied joint to joint a frame or two later; poses keyed on every control at each main pose with an anticipation before and a settle after. The build measures every clip and fails if a toe goes under the ground, a limb stretches past 8%, or a planted toe leaves its line by 3 mm. Clips are named for a pack's bricks: sniff and sniff_air for world.scent_field's two nose modes, drag for movement.carry_in_mouth's heavy things, dig and lie for housing.den_and_cache, bark and mark for the two inputs that lay or drop scent. The course and its squirrel are a reference and never an asset.
